reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a flash-loan arbitrage bot as a way to earn BNB and instructs viewers to deploy a contract, connect a wallet, and send BNB to it before executing repeated transactions. It also claims that a specified retry configuration should work 100%, pairing a financial-return promise with required fund transfers and operational steps.

citations.quote: How to Earn BNB STEP BY STEP
Today we bring you a zero coding needed flash loan arbitrage bot!
Send BNB to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.2+
Send cash money over to the contract address to run it
This is to run the smart loan contractor just makes them and click on action.

opening.argument: Judge, the presentation does not describe a risk-free source of BNB. It explains that a flash loan must be repaid within the same transaction and warns that flash-loan exploits have stolen money. It also acknowledges that the contract may fail with low amounts and that an attempted arbitrage might fail. Those qualifications support reading the video as a technical walkthrough with stated limitations, rather than an unconditional promise of returns.

citations.quote: A flash loan has to be borrowed and repaid within the same blockchain transaction.
flash loan exploits have been used to attack vulnerable DeFi protocols and steal millions of dollars.
Avoid using very low amounts as contract may fail below 0.15 BNB.
the arbitrage might fail due to depletion of BNB in your smart contract

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited instruction to send BNB establishes that funding is part of the demonstrated procedure; it does not, by itself, establish where those funds ultimately go or whether the contract can perform the described operation. The opening also treats the earnings framing as a guarantee, overlooking the video's express discussion of failed transactions.

citations.quote: Send BNB to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.2+
the arbitrage might fail due to depletion of BNB in your smart contract

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The warnings do not resolve the central concern: viewers are instructed to send BNB to a contract built from linked code before running it. The description then tells them to send more BNB if the first attempt fails and claims a retry configuration should work 100%. A warning about possible failure does not substantiate the bot's promised earning mechanism or make the funding instruction benign.

citations.quote: Name the file flashloans.sol and paste the contract code link below.
Send BNB to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.2+
if it doesn't work with 0.2 BNB try to send another 0.2 BNB
it should work 100% but with a smaller profit.

opening.argument: Judge, the video devotes its explanation to a reproducible software workflow: creating a Solidity file, selecting the compiler, deploying a contract and invoking its function. The speaker even corrects their description of which network the contract was launched on. The claim about an amount made appears within that demonstration; the supplied material does not independently establish the amount as profit, but neither does that uncertainty turn every depicted software step into a solicitation. The central observable activity is instruction in using the tools.

citations.quote: make a new file so you can go to create a new file give the file a name
We want 0, 5, 0. So I'm going here and we're going to pick.
oh no not pancake swap we launched it on the b&b smart chain
Look at that amount we just made.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening accurately identifies the wallet and funding steps, but those steps are also part of what the speaker demonstrates after deployment. The quoted instruction says the transfer is to run the contract; it does not show the contract's code executing or establish the recipient's control over the funds. The video can contain an unverified earnings claim while still being primarily a tool demonstration.

citations.quote: We're going to copy that go to send paste in your new contract address
Send cash money over to the contract address to run it

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The workflow is precisely how the promoted earning scheme is presented to viewers. The title offers a way to earn BNB, the description supplies external contract code, and the instructions require sending BNB to the deployed contract. Demonstrating the clicks does not make the financial pitch incidental, especially when the speaker claims to have made an amount without establishing actual profit.

citations.quote: How to Earn BNB STEP BY STEP
Name the file flashloans.sol and paste the contract code link below.
Send BNB to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.2+
Look at that amount we just made.

opening.argument: Judge, the described transaction is funding a newly deployed contract to run a proposed arbitrage operation, not an identified payment to the creator. The speaker tells viewers to copy their new contract address, and the description tells them to transfer BNB out to another wallet afterward. Those details leave material questions unanswered: the supplied record does not show who controls the contract's funds, what the linked code actually does, or whether the claimed result is a net gain. The funding step warrants scrutiny, but an instruction to fund a contract does not alone establish a diversion of funds.

citations.quote: copy that go to send paste in your new contract address
Send BNB to the deployed contract to initiate the swap 0.2+
Make sure to transfer your BNB out to another wallet when you're done.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening establishes a promoted bot, a required BNB transfer and an aggressive success claim. It does not establish that the new contract address belongs to the speaker or that a transfer to it is irrecoverable. The speaker describes copying the newly launched contract's address, while the description contemplates moving BNB out afterward. The actual disposition of funds remains unshown.

citations.quote: there's our new contract we.
copy that go to send paste in your new contract address
Make sure to transfer your BNB out to another wallet when you're done.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A transfer-out instruction is not evidence that withdrawal works. The video directs viewers to paste linked code, deploy it and send BNB to the resulting contract, while offering an earnings pitch and a retry said to work 100%. The supplied material need not show a completed loss to support concern about this funded-contract promotion; it also does not verify the code, withdrawal ability or actual profit.
